title: Session
description: Metadata schema for a recorded gameplay session.

oneOf.description: Camera Rotation (Speed-Based): Raw mouse deltas turn the character's head or rotate the 3D viewport. Faster movement equals faster rotation. Cursor is usually locked and hidden. Examples: Call of Duty, Halo, Elden Ring.

Camera Translation (Speed-Based): Moving the mouse or dragging across the screen slides the entire camera anchor linearly across a flat 2D plane or map. Examples: StarCraft, Age of Empires, Cities: Skylines.

Camera Direction (Absolute Position-Based): The absolute screen coordinates of the mouse dictate the camera's movement or tilt. Common in edge-scrolling or virtual joystick flight setups. Examples: Microsoft Flight Simulator, strategy edge-panning.

2D Interface Pointer (Absolute Position-Based): The mouse controls a visible, free-roaming screen cursor used to click UI buttons, manage inventories, or select items. Examples: Monkey Island, League of Legends menus.

Mechanical Control Mapping: Mouse movement mimics a physical steering wheel, flight yoke, or handlebars to turn a vehicle rather than just controlling a camera viewpoint. Examples: War Thunder aircraft, GTA driving.
No Mouse Interaction: Mouse input is entirely disregarded by the game engine during primary gameplay. Examples: Fighting games (Mortal Kombat), pure gamepad/keyboard platformers.

Custom/Unique Interaction: The mouse drives an entirely custom mechanic not covered by the standard options. Note: Requires 'maps_to_other' to be populated. Examples: Mouse gestures for spellcasting, lockpicking mini-games.

vendor_name.description: Name of the vendor who captured and delivered the data.

game_title.description: Title of the game being played.

created_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp when the session recording began (timezone-aware ISO 8601, e.g. '2026-06-15T10:00:00Z').

ended_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp when the session recording ended (timezone-aware ISO 8601, e.g. '2026-06-15T11:00:00Z').

duration_ms.description: Total duration of the recording in milliseconds.

duration_seconds.description: Total duration of the recording in seconds.

fps.description: Frames per second of the recording.

frame_count.description: Total number of frames in the recording.

record_width_px.description: Width of the recorded video in pixels.

record_height_px.description: Height of the recorded video in pixels.

screen_width_px.description: Width of the source screen/display in pixels.

screen_height_px.description: Height of the source screen/display in pixels.

localization.description: BCP 47 language tag representing the locale of the session (e.g. 'en-US', 'ja-JP').

platform.description: The gaming platform on which the session was recorded.

maps_to.description: Indicates the primary system or camera quantity driven by raw mouse inputs during the main gameplay mode of the session. When behavior varies within the session, this is the predominant mapping; deviations are declared in input_mouse_convention_segments.

maps_to_other.description: Mandatory human-readable string clarifying the specific behavior if 'maps_to' is set to 'other'.

dx_positive.description: Camera/view response to a positive input_mouse_dx delta (moving physical mouse to player's right). Reflects actual in-session settings as observed from the player's perspective.

dx_negative.description: Camera/view response to a negative input_mouse_dx delta (moving physical mouse to player's left). Reflects actual in-session settings as observed from the player's perspective.

dy_positive.description: Camera/view response to positive input_mouse_dy -- moving the physical mouse down (towards player's body). Captures whether invert-Y was enabled.

dy_negative.description: Camera/view response to negative input_mouse_dy -- moving the physical mouse up (away from player's body). Captures whether invert-Y was enabled.

input_mouse_convention.description: Declares what the raw mouse deltas control (maps_to) and, for active camera control mappings, the directional/inversion convention. The predominant mapping for the session; see input_mouse_convention_segments for within-session deviations.

input_mouse_convention_segments.description: Optional. Declares frame ranges where the mouse-to-camera/game behavior deviates from the session-level input_mouse_convention.maps_to (e.g. GTA: on-foot camera_look_velocity session with a vehicle_steering segment while driving). Frames not covered by any segment are governed by the session-level mapping. Segments must not overlap. Frame indices are 0-based and align with frames.csv row order; start_frame is inclusive, end_frame is exclusive.

start_frame.description: First frame of the segment (inclusive, 0-based, aligned with frames.csv).

end_frame.description: Frame after the last frame of the segment (exclusive, 0-based, aligned with frames.csv).

maps_to.description: Mouse-to-camera/game behavior in effect during this segment.

maps_to_other.description: Mandatory human-readable string clarifying the specific behavior if this segment's 'maps_to' is set to 'other'.
